clue.text: Origin and end of Arethusa

definitions.meaning: a source or wellhead from which something springs
in Greek myth the nymph Arethusa finished her story transformed into a spring of water

explanation.surface: A classical scholar asks where the nymph Arethusa came from and how her story finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellspring is a source, and in myth the nymph Arethusa was changed into a spring at Syracuse.

clue.text: Feeble young creature reared by detectives

indicators.note: in a down clue, reared means raised up, so the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a calf is a young cow
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's police detectives

explanation.surface: A weak young animal has been brought up by police officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaccid means limp and lacking firmness, a synonym of weak.

clue.text: This Head assumed to be an easy liar, do we hear?

definitions.text: This Head assumed to be an easy liar, do we hear?

parts.words: This Head assumed to be an easy liar, do we hear?
parts.note: Shakespeare wrote 'uneasy lies the head that wears a crown', so a head without one would lie easy, sounding like an easy liar

explanation.surface: A question about whether a certain leader is thought to tell lies readily.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is from Henry IV Part 2; 'liar' plays on 'lies' in the sense of lying down to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A head without a crown escapes the worry Shakespeare's line gives to kings, so it rests easily.

clue.text: Irksome to be ordered outside

indicators.note: ordered means put into a fresh arrangement, so the letters of the next word are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Being told to go outdoors is annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges OUTSIDE; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious means boring and tiresome, which is what irksome describes.

clue.text: Senselessness of batting on it in any circumstances

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in

indicators.note: in places the word it inside the word any

explanation.surface: Batting on regardless, whatever happens, is a senseless thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batting' is the cricket sense: the side batting is 'in'. 'on' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanity is silliness or lack of sense, a synonym of senselessness.

clue.text: Rural areas lacking right to a Territorial division

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is removed from the word for rural areas

parts.note: the country is the countryside away from towns

explanation.surface: Country areas without a right to their own Territorial Army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was Britain's volunteer reserve, but here 'Territorial division' just means an area of land; a COUNTY is a British administrative region.
explanation.definitionFit: A county is an administrative area, one of the regions a country is split into.

clue.text: Castle governor commits schedule to memory

parts.note: to con, with 'to memory' completing the sense, is to learn by heart
a timetable or table is a schedule

explanation.surface: The man in charge of a castle learns the timetable by heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commits ... to memory' gives CONS, an old word for studying or learning by heart; the 'to memory' half is split from it by 'schedule'.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a constable was the officer in charge of a royal castle, as at the Tower of London.

clue.text: Free tea in Union? No, love

indicators.note: in places the word for tea inside what remains
no here means without, so the letter for love is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, written as O
cha is a colloquial word for tea

explanation.surface: A union official offers free tea, but no love comes with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' tells you to drop love's letter from the union word, leaving UNIN; the union is a trade union in the surface, but here it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To unchain is to release, a verb sense of set free.

clue.text: Cooks boast about a bit of hot stuff

indicators.note: to cook is to doctor or tamper with, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Kitchen staff brag about a hot dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooks' rearranges BOAST with C and A; 'Cooks' looks like the subject of the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a fiery pepper sauce, a small dash of something very hot.

clue.text: Cloth worker once had car damaged

indicators.note: damaged means wrecked, so the letters of the preceding words are reshaped

explanation.surface: A textile worker of the past had a car smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cloth' means the clergy, so a cloth worker is a churchman, not a weaver.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloth is a term for the clergy, and an archdeacon is a senior Anglican clergyman.

clue.text: Hector's mother an ambassador to this island?

indicators.note: to here joins the ambassador's letters to the island, so taking them away from the mother's name leaves the island

parts.note: in the Iliad, Hecuba is queen of Troy and mother of Hector
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: Might Hector's mother be sent as envoy to some island?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: Hector's mother's name reads as an ambassador's title followed by the island, so 'to' links the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Hollow grief when a carnivore causes lacerations

parts.note: a crocodile is a meat-eating reptile
tears are rips or cuts

explanation.surface: Feigned mourning while a predator mauls its prey.
explanation.walkthrough: TEARS here rhymes with 'bears', not with 'fears'.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocodile tears are insincere sorrow, from the old belief that crocodiles weep while eating.

clue.text: Extremely dodgy and disagreeable line of- succession

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the next word, its first and last letters

parts.note: nasty means unpleasant or disagreeable

explanation.surface: A family's line of heirs described as shifty and unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray hyphen after 'of' is a printing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynasty is a series of rulers from one family, passing power down the generations.

clue.text: Object straddling watercourse, causing sensation

indicators.note: straddling means sitting astride, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a thing is an object
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: Something lying across a stream causes a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrilling means exciting, producing a strong sensation of excitement.

clue.text: Letting oneself go on following a group

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the word on is placed after the other pieces

parts.note: a band is a group of people or musicians

explanation.surface: Losing one's inhibitions while touring with a pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandon is unrestrained freedom of manner, as in dancing with abandon.

clue.text: Croatian in a spotted coat

definitions.meaning: from the coastal region of Croatia on the Adriatic
describing a breed of dog with a white coat covered in black spots

explanation.surface: A Croatian man wearing a spotty jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalmatia is a region of Croatia, and its name is given to the spotted dog breed.

clue.text: Wine produced by some republicans

parts.note: made means produced
the IRA, the Irish Republican Army, is a group of republicans

explanation.surface: A wine made by members of a republican movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a fortified wine from the Portuguese island of the same name.

clue.text: Boy twice goes on a forage

indicators.note: twice means the boy's name appears two times in a row

parts.note: Alf is a boy's name, short for Alfred

explanation.surface: A boy goes out twice to forage for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forage' looks like a verb but is the noun: animal fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfalfa, or lucerne, is a plant grown as fodder for livestock.

clue.text: It'S quite enough to support former model

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits underneath, so it follows the other piece

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
ample means plenty or quite enough

explanation.surface: Plenty of money goes to support a former fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link; 'former model' looks like one phrase but splits into the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a pattern to copy, a sense shared with model.

clue.text: Lay going on for ages

definitions.meaning: lasting through the centuries, from Latin saeculum, an age

explanation.surface: Something that has gone on for a long time without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Secular means non-religious, like lay people, and in an older sense lasting for an age or more.

clue.text: He learns about horses — a specialist area

parts.note: a stud is an establishment of horses kept for breeding
ENT, ear nose and throat, is a medical specialty

explanation.surface: A man learns about horses as his specialist subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A student is someone studying, one who learns.

clue.text: Lombardy's turbulent romance

definitions.note: a possessive standing for a place in that region: one of Lombardy's cities

indicators.note: turbulent means stormy or disordered, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A stormy love affair in northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremona is a city in the Lombardy region of Italy, famous for violin-making.

clue.text: An excellent specimen of the Crotalidae family

definitions.meaning: a cracking good example of something, in old slang
a pit viper with a noisy tail of horny rings

explanation.surface: A fine example of a snake from the pit viper family.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattler is informal for something first-rate and also short for rattlesnake, a pit viper.

clue.text: Iris Cassio, for instance, the Admiral's helper

parts.note: the yellow flag is a kind of iris
Cassio is Othello's lieutenant in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: Characters named Iris and Cassio help the admiral.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag lieutenant is the aide-de-camp to an admiral in the navy.

clue.text: Aileron causing panic

definitions.meaning: a hinged surface on an aircraft wing

explanation.surface: A wing part on a plane causing alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is a movable flap on a wing, and a flap is also a fluster or state of panic.

clue.text: The moan of doves in — elms" (Tennyson)

definitions.text: The moan of doves in — elms" (Tennyson)

parts.words: The moan of doves in — elms" (Tennyson)
parts.note: fill the gap in a line from Tennyson's poem The Princess with the adjective he gives the elms

explanation.surface: A quotation from Tennyson with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The full line is 'The moan of doves in ... elms, / And murmuring of innumerable bees'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means ancient beyond memory, describing the old elms.

clue.text: Ne'er-do-well gave instruction to Governor-General

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, to command

explanation.surface: A good-for-nothing gave orders to the Governor-General.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad egg is an idiom for a worthless or untrustworthy person.

clue.text: Composer runs inside for a device to catch leaves

indicators.note: inside places the abbreviation for runs within the composer's name

parts.note: Sir John Stainer was an English composer of church music
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A composer goes indoors to find something for catching leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' means tea leaves, not those falling from trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea strainer is a small sieve that catches the leaves as tea is poured.
